questions.question: What is the main purpose of this topic?

options.text: To prepare, understand, or evaluate data and models using the methods covered in the lesson
To guarantee that every model is correct
To replace all reasoning with a single metric
To avoid testing code

questions.explanation: The methods support a reproducible workflow but cannot guarantee perfect results.

questions.question: Which practice is most important for a trustworthy workflow?

options.text: Inspect data and keep evaluation data separate from fitting and tuning
Tune repeatedly on the final test set
Ignore missing values
Choose a method based only on its name

questions.explanation: Data inspection and separation of fitting from evaluation reduce errors and overly optimistic estimates.

questions.question: What should you do when results are surprising?

options.text: Check assumptions, data types, shapes, and a small reproducible example
Immediately discard the data
Report the best-looking result only
Assume the library is wrong

questions.explanation: A systematic check is more reliable than guessing or selectively reporting results.

questions.question: Why is a baseline useful?

options.text: It provides a simple reference against which a more complex method can be compared
It proves the complex method is unnecessary in every task
It guarantees high accuracy
It eliminates the need for a test set

questions.explanation: A baseline contextualizes performance and helps determine whether added complexity is worthwhile.

questions.question: Which statement about sample or model results is correct?

options.text: Results should be interpreted with their assumptions and limitations
A single result always proves causation
Synthetic examples prove deployment performance
A high score removes all uncertainty

questions.explanation: Evidence must be interpreted in context; toy data and single scores have limited scope.
